title: Introduce compact credential scheduler and align stream retry profiles across SDKs
author: Claire Nguyen
release_notes:
- Adds a compact credential scheduler shared by Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to reduce reauth jitter and duplicate refreshes.
- Harmonizes streaming retry presets and heartbeat/backoff defaults across SDKs.
- Small ergonomics improvements to credential provider interfaces and a migration guide.
body:
Background and motivation: We continue to see customer telemetry showing bursts of near-simultaneous credential refreshes from multi-threaded clients and short-lived connections. Those refresh bursts increase load spikes against the auth service, and in edge cases can cause transient stream drops while SDKs independently backoff and retry. This PR introduces a lightweight, compact credential scheduler (a small local coordinator in each SDK) plus a synchronized set of streaming retry profiles that reduce reconnect churn and improve cross-language parity. The goal is better out-of-the-box stability for short-lived streams and more predictable unit economics for high-concurrency clients.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds compact credential scheduler implementations in Python/TypeScript/Go (sdk helpers only). The scheduler batches/defers refreshes, applies jitter windows, and exposes a minimal contract for external credential providers to implement (observe/refresh).
- Standardizes streaming retry profiles across SDKs: short, balanced, and conservative presets with explicit default values for: initial_delay, max_delay, multiplier, max_retries, and heartbeat_window.
- Updates streaming connection handshake to consult the SDK-level scheduler for credential validity before attempting reconnects (reduces back-to-back auth failures).
- Backfills unit tests and e2e smoke tests that exercise cross-language behavior under load via the existing harness.
- Adds a short migration guide in docs/sdk-migration/credential_scheduler.md and updates the TypeScript and Python changelogs.

Design notes:
- The credential scheduler is intentionally minimal: it does not centralize network calls across processes, only within an SDK instance. It is safe to use in multi-threaded and event-loop contexts. The API surface is one small trait/interface (observe, refresh_if_needed) plus an optional background wake hook.
- Retry presets were chosen after analyzing production disconnect histograms; they aim to reduce rapid reconnect storms while keeping recovery latency acceptable for interactive apps.

Checklist:
- [x] Feature in Python SDK: compact scheduler and tests (redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/cred_scheduler.py).
- [x] Feature in TypeScript SDK: compact scheduler and tests (redwood-sdk-typescript/src/cred/scheduler.ts).
- [x] Feature in Go SDK: compact scheduler and tests (redwood-sdk-go/cred/scheduler.go).
- [x] Cross-language docs and migration guide.
- [x] E2E smoke tests added to benchmark-lab/e2e/cred-burst.test.
- [x] CI green and manual canary run on staging.

Commits (high level):
- feat(sdk): add compact credential scheduler interface and Python implementation
- feat(sdk): add TypeScript scheduler, unit tests, and typings
- feat(sdk): add Go scheduler and concurrency tests
- chore(sdk): introduce shared retry_profiles.yaml and loader in SDK build pipeline
- docs: add migration guide and changelog entries
- test: add e2e scenario for credential burst and streaming reconnect stability

Files changed (representative):
- redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/cred_scheduler.py (+210)
- redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_cred_scheduler.py (+84)
- redwood-sdk-typescript/src/cred/scheduler.ts (+196)
- redwood-sdk-typescript/tests/scheduler.spec.ts (+98)
- redwood-sdk-go/cred/scheduler.go (+132)
- redwood-sdk-go/cred/scheduler_test.go (+74)
- shared/retry_profiles.yaml (+36)
- docs/sdk-migration/credential_scheduler.md (+12)
- benchmark-lab/e2e/cred-burst.test (+24)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Samir Patel (reviewer): "Nice compact design. Two asks: 1) please call out that the scheduler does not try to deduplicate refreshes across processes, and 2) include an opt-out flag for users who want strict per-request refresh behavior."
  - Author (Claire Nguyen): "Added explicit note in the design doc and an opt-out config 'cred_scheduler=disabled' for advanced users. Also added tests to validate opt-out behavior."
- Asha Kumar (reviewer): "Can we tighten the TypeScript types so the scheduler works with older TS targets? We saw CI compile warnings."
  - Author: "Adjusted build targets and added a -lib fallback. Verified compilation on TS 4.6 in CI matrix."
- Miguel Santos (reviewer): "Go concurrency looks good but please make sure the scheduler's background ticker respects ctx cancellation (I left a small nits comment)."
  - Author: "Fixed: background ticker now listens to ctx.Done() and we added a test to ensure goroutines don't leak after shutdown."

CI and testing summary:
- Unit tests: all SDK unit suites passed in parallel (py/ts/go).
- Lint: TypeScript lint fixed after adding rule exceptions for the small helper.
- Integration/E2E: benchmark-lab/cred-burst runs showed a 62% reduction in simultaneous auth refresh requests in the staging harness.
- Flaky tests: one intermittent TS test (session reconnect spec) failed on initial run; we patched the test to stabilize timing and CI reran. Final CI status: PASS.

Manual verification and canary:
- Deployed to the 'sdk-canary' environment and exercised with the in-house burst tool. Observed fewer reconnects and a 15% reduction in per-minute reconnects under the simulated load. No customer-visible regressions reported during the alpha window.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Default behavior unchanged for consumers: scheduler is enabled by default but keeps the original credential provider contract. If consumers relied on per-request immediate refresh side-effects, they can opt out by setting cred_scheduler=disabled OR implementing the explicit 'force_refresh' hint on their provider. Migration guide included in docs.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: scheduler hides a rare provider-side error until next scheduled window. Mitigation: scheduler surfaces refresh failures through metrics and keeps a short retry window for transient errors; we also recommend provider implementations surface critical failures immediately via the existing callback.
- Risk: subtle timing differences between SDKs. Mitigation: retry_profiles.yaml provides consistent defaults; future work may introduce a telemetry-safe cross-sdk experiment to tune defaults per region.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-24 after reviewers approved (Samir/Asha/Miguel) and CI green. Release notes added to the SDK changelogs and internal announcement posted in #sdk-platform.

Related work: ENG-1452 (credential stability initiative), ENG-1487 (streaming retry harmonization).

If reviewers want incremental follow-ups:
- Follow-up: Add a lightweight telemetry metric for scheduler-induced refresh deferrals (ENG-1520).
- Follow-up: Evaluate cross-process coordination approaches for large single-host deployments (design spike).

If you need to reproduce the canary run: see benchmark-lab/e2e/README and run `make e2e-cred-burst` against the staging cluster.

-- Claire Nguyen (author)
